rawItems.content: Residents are being asked to help decide where a new zebra crossing should be installed in Ramsey as part of plans to improve pedestrian safety and accessibility in the town. Cambridgeshire County Council is asking residents to choose between two possible sites for the crossing. The proposed locations are: Residents have two sites to choose from one is on High Street, opposite Ramsey Abbey Gatehouse, the other is on Hollow Lane opposite Ramsey Golf and Bowls Club. (Image: Google Maps / Street View) The council said the results of the survey, which runs until midnight on Wednesday, October 28, will be considered alongside other highway, safety and accessibility information before a final decision is made. Residents, students, parents, carers and regular pedestrians are all being encouraged to take part. The council says residents’ views will help identify the safest and most effective site for people travelling on foot. Places for People Living+ Limited has applied to Huntingdonshire District Council for prior approval to demolish Suffolk House, Grenville House, 10 bungalows and 32 garages off Suffolk Close, Huntingdon. Documents lodged with the council state that the buildings are currently vacant and that their removal is required to enable the wider redevelopment of the site for residential purposes. The application proposes demolition beginning on January 5, 2027. Planning documents indicate the works could be completed by April 2, 2027. Primary access to the site is off Suffolk Close via Mayfield Road, the A141 and A1. rawItems.title: 5 long lost railway stations in Cambridgeshire you may not have heard of
rawItems.content: Cambridgeshire's railway network was once far larger than it is today, with long-lost stations serving market towns, villages and growing industrial centres across the county. While many have since disappeared, their stories remain woven into the landscape, offering fascinating reminders of a very different age of travel. Before Peterborough became synonymous with the East Coast Main Line, the city's first railway station was Peterborough East. Opened in 1845 by the Eastern Counties Railway, it served routes towards Northampton, Rugby, March, Wisbech and Norwich. The station was known simply as Peterborough until being renamed Peterborough East in 1923. Passenger services ended in June 1966 as part of wider railway cutbacks, although the site continued handling parcels traffic until 1970. Today, little remains apart from the historic engine sheds, but the former station played a crucial role in shaping Peterborough's growth into a major railway city. Ramsey was once unusual in having two separate railway stations. Ramsey North opened in 1863 as the terminus of the Ramsey Railway branch from Holme. The line was worked by the Great Northern Railway and connected the market town with the wider national network. Renamed Ramsey North in 1923, the station struggled to attract large passenger numbers, particularly as road transport became more popular during the twentieth century. Passenger services ceased in October 1947, although freight traffic continued for many years afterwards

rawItems.title: Ramsey builder named Builder of the Year for Midlands and Wales
rawItems.content: A Ramsey builder has been named Builder of the Year at the Checkatrade Regional Awards. Liam Hilbrown of Carter’s Restoration Services received the honour for the Midlands and Wales region at a ceremony held earlier this month at the Wolverhampton Wanderers Stadium. The awards celebrate tradespeople who demonstrate not only exceptional craftsmanship but also professionalism and reliability. Jambu Palaniappan, CEO of Checkatrade, said: "Great trades earn their place on Checkatrade and keep earning it. "But members like Liam Hilbrown go a step beyond this already high bar. "The Checkatrade Awards are all about celebrating the pride and effort our outstanding members put into their work, and shining a light on their achievements. "We’re very proud of them all." Winners are chosen from more than 2,500 nominations nationwide. Checkatrade sets a rigorous entry standard for its members, requiring up to 12 checks before joining and ongoing monitoring through customer feedback. The awards will conclude with a national final in London on November 19, where regional winners will compete for national honours.
